segments.spoken_text: 1. Overview and Design Principles

chunks.text:
1. Overview and Design Principles.

The Software Cloud publishing platform is engineered around strict computational determinism, reproducibility, and security. Built upon Jupyter Book 2 (JB2) and the MyST Markdown ecosystem, every component—from environment dependency resolution to static HTML artifact generation—is verified before deployment.

segments.spoken_text: Core Architectural Tenants

Deterministic Dependency Locking: All runtime Python distributions and their transitive dependencies are pinned with exact versions and cryptographic SHA-256 digests (--require-hashes, --only-binary=:all:). Canonical Execution Environment: Builds and notebook executions target CPython 3.12.14 on Linux x86-64, isolating execution state and preventing architecture drift. Explicit Profile Validation: A standalone preflight validator (tools/check_profile.py) enforces schema integrity, kernelspec registration, TOC exhaustiveness, and execution control compliance prior to artifact compilation. Reproducible Continuous Delivery: GitHub Actions runs the verified pipeline in an isolated runner, builds the static publication artifact under --strict mode, and deploys to my.softcloud.dev.

segments.spoken_text: 2. Repository Layout & Topology
The repository follows a clean, minimal directory topology designed for auditability:

This file tree outlines the project structure for the soft-cloud-dev repository, establishing a standardized environment for documentation publishing, dependency management, and automated continuous integration. The root directory contains configuration files for a Jupyter Book 2 project, driven by the myst.yml configuration and the top-level introduction and architecture Markdown files, alongside custom domain mapping and BSD 2-Clause licensing. Core functionality and tooling reside in the tools directory, featuring a hermetic publication build runner shell script, a profile compliance and integrity validator, and a wheelhouse hash resolver that generates cryptographically pinned lockfiles from requirements.in to requirements.lock. Computational elements are isolated within the notebooks directory through a verified CPython 3.12.14 experiment notebook, while branding assets like favicons and scalable vector graphics logos are maintained in the images directory to support both light and dark display modes. Automated delivery is managed by a GitHub Actions workflow in the dot github workflows directory, handling CI/CD deployment. Implementation decisions emphasize reproducibility and security through strict dependency pinning, hermetic builds, and artifact exclusions via gitignore. Potential risks include build failures if the pinned wheelhouse hashes drift from the top-level dependency declarations or if the CPython execution environment within the notebook falls out of sync with the locked package versions.

segments.spoken_text: 3.2. .gitignore
Strict exclusion rules keep local cache artifacts, wheelhouses, and virtual environments outside source control:

This text block defines a standard ignore file configuration, such as a Gitignore file, for a Python-based Software Cloud project. Its primary purpose is to specify local development directories, virtual environments, build artifacts, and cache folders that should be excluded from version control. The configuration lists common transient directories, including local virtual environments under point venv and point lock venv, local package wheelhouse archives, documentation or source build outputs under underscore build, Python bytecode caches under double underscore pycache double underscore, and Jupyter Notebook checkpoint directories. By excluding these paths, the configuration prevents environment-specific binaries, temporary cache files, and local build states from being tracked or committed to the repository. The implementation relies on pattern matching against standard Python and Jupyter tooling directories. The primary side effect of applying these rules is that local development dependencies and compiled caches will not be shared across environments, ensuring clean, reproducible deployments while requiring developers to regenerate virtual environments and build assets locally.

segments.spoken_text: 3.5. Computational Notebook: notebooks/experiment.ipynb
An executable verification notebook executed by Jupyter Book during the build process to guarantee runtime environment health:

This JSON document defines a Jupyter notebook structured for computational verification and environment runtime validation on the Software Cloud platform. Operating under format version four point five, the notebook targets a specific Python kernel designated as jb2-python, matching version three point twelve point fourteen. The notebook contains two cells: an introductory markdown cell outlining the verification purpose, and a single code cell dependent on the sys module. The code cell outputs the current Python executable path and full version string to standard out, and includes an explicit assertion checking that the active interpreter matches version three point twelve point fourteen precisely. A limitation of this implementation is that the hardcoded version assertion will trigger an AssertionError and halt execution if run in any environment other than the exact specified patch release.

segments.spoken_text: 4. Build & Maintenance Toolchain
4.1. Lockfile Generator: tools/lock_from_wheels.py
This maintenance utility resolves wheel archives in .wheelhouse/, extracts their normalized distribution metadata, computes their SHA-256 checksums, and produces a strictly pinned requirements.lock:

This Python script generates a Pip-compatible requirements file with cryptographic hashes from a directory of pre-downloaded wheel files. It accepts two command-line arguments representing the input wheelhouse directory and the output requirements file path, depending on standard libraries including zipfile, hashlib, and email. The script validates that the output file does not already exist to prevent accidental overwrites, ensures the input directory contains exclusively wheel files, and verifies that each wheel contains unambiguous metadata. It parses the package name and version from each wheel's METADATA file, standardizes the distribution name, checks for duplicate packages, and computes a SHA-256 file digest for integrity verification. Finally, it writes sorted, pinned requirement strings containing the package name, version, and hash to the output file using exclusive creation mode. Potential risks include runtime termination via SystemExit if any validation checks fail, such as missing wheels, unexpected directory contents, ambiguous metadata, or duplicate distributions.

segments.spoken_text: This Python script performs a strict preflight validation check for a Jupyter Book project configured with a MyST Markdown structure. Its purpose is to ensure the execution environment, package dependencies, environment variables, configuration files, table of contents, and notebooks strictly adhere to required specifications before building the documentation. The script relies on standard libraries such as json, os, re, sys, and pathlib, alongside external dependencies including PyYAML and the Jupyter Client package. It begins by validating that the runtime is CPython version 3.12.14, running inside an active virtual environment, and that specific core packages like jupyter-book and ipykernel match exact version pins. It enforces clean environment variables by rejecting unexpected overrides like Jupyter tokens or base URLs, while requiring an explicit and securely formatted BASE_URL. Next, the script checks the local Jupyter kernel registration to ensure it targets the correct Python interpreter and is not shadowed by an external spec. It then parses the myst.yml configuration file, confirming version one compliance, ensuring no unauthorized inheritance, plugins, or exclusions are present, and validating that a nonempty table of contents and the correct book-theme selector are defined. The script recursively walks the table of contents to verify that every entry references a valid local file safely contained within the working directory, with no duplicate files allowed. It also ensures that all notebook files located on disk are explicitly accounted for within the table of contents. Finally, the script inspects both the configuration and all referenced notebooks and Markdown files for banned execution controls, such as skipped executions, raised exceptions, or restricted tags. It validates that any computational notebook or document containing executable directives correctly binds to the required jupyter kernel named jb2-python. It also rejects legacy configuration files like underscore config or underscore toc yaml. The primary side effect of this script is that it terminates execution via a system exit call with a descriptive error message if any validation constraint fails, preventing misconfigured builds. Upon successful completion, it outputs a success message indicating the total number of verified table of contents files.

segments.spoken_text: 4.3. Hermetic Build Runner: tools/build.sh
The shell script orchestrating preflight validation, cache purging, and strict compilation:

This POSIX shell script automates the validation, building, and verification process for a Jupyter Book project within the Software Cloud platform. It operates under strict error-handling rules, exiting immediately on any command failure or unbound variable usage, and explicitly disables external Node environment management via the JB_ALLOW_NODEENV environment variable. The script begins by verifying that essential runtime dependencies are installed and accessible in the system path, specifically checking Node.js, npm, Python, and the Python package manager pip. It then executes a custom Python profile validation script located in the tools directory, checks the installed Jupyter Book version, and performs a clean build of the documentation. During the build phase, it executes notebooks in strict mode to catch runtime errors within the documentation source files. Finally, the script validates the output by asserting that the primary HTML index file is successfully generated and non-empty. The primary material side effects include modifying the local filesystem by clearing previous build artifacts, executing potentially untrusted notebook code during the build process, and generating a new set of static HTML files in the local directory.

segments.spoken_text: 5. Continuous Deployment: .github/workflows/deploy.yml
The CI/CD pipeline deploys the publication to GitHub Pages on every push to main:

This GitHub Actions workflow automates the building and deployment of a Jupyter Book to GitHub Pages. It triggers automatically on pushes to the main branch or via manual workflow dispatch, running exclusively on the main branch to secure the production environment. The configuration consists of two sequential jobs. The build job runs on Ubuntu 24.04 and requires read permissions for repository contents and pages. It checks out the repository, configures GitHub Pages, and sets up CPython version 3.12.14. It then creates a virtual environment and securely installs dependencies from a requirements.lock file using strict hash checking and binary-only constraints. It registers an IPython kernel and executes a custom build script located at tools/build.sh, which outputs HTML files into the underscore build html directory. Finally, it uploads this directory as a GitHub Pages build artifact. The deploy job depends directly on the successful completion of the build job. Running with write permissions for pages and identity tokens, it publishes the uploaded artifact to the GitHub Pages environment, making the site publicly accessible at the generated deployment URL. Concurrency is configured to group page deployments and prevent overlapping cancellations.

segments.spoken_text: 6. Deterministic Dependency Resolution
To guarantee binary compatibility with the Ubuntu CI runner, requirements.lock was generated inside a Linux/x86-64 container hosting CPython 3.12.14:

chunks.text:
6. Deterministic Dependency Resolution.

To guarantee binary compatibility with the Ubuntu CI runner, requirements.lock was generated inside a Linux/x86-64 container hosting CPython 3.12.14:

segments.spoken_text: This shell script automates the generation of a reproducible dependency lock file for Python projects within the Software Cloud platform. Its primary purpose is to pre-download binary wheels for all requirements specified in requirements.in and transform them into a pinned lock file without installing them into the host environment. The execution begins by creating a temporary Python 3.12 virtual environment named dot-lock-venv and a temporary directory named dot-wheelhouse. It then invokes pip within the virtual environment to download strictly pre-compiled binary packages for everything listed in requirements.in, saving the resulting wheels to the wheelhouse directory. Following the download phase, a custom utility script located at tools/lock_from_wheels.py parses the local wheelhouse to generate a deterministic requirements.lock file. Finally, the script performs a cleanup operation, recursively removing both the temporary virtual environment and the wheelhouse directory. Significant inputs include the requirements.in configuration file and the lock_from_wheels.py parsing tool, while the primary output is the generated requirements.lock file. Key dependencies are Python 3.12, the pip package manager, and network access to retrieve the packages. A notable implementation decision is the use of an isolated virtual environment and the strict enforcement of binary-only downloads, ensuring consistency across different deployment architectures. Material side effects are limited to the creation and subsequent deletion of temporary local directories and files during the build process. A potential risk is that the script will fail if network access is unavailable, if packages lack compatible pre-compiled binary wheels, or if Python 3.12 is not present in the execution environment.

4. Build & Maintenance Toolchain
4.1. Lockfile Generator: tools/lock_from_wheels.py
This maintenance utility resolves wheel archives in .wheelhouse/, extracts their normalized distribution metadata, computes their SHA-256 checksums, and produces a strictly pinned requirements.lock:

import email
import hashlib
import re
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

wheelhouse, output = map(Path, sys.argv[1:])
if output.exists():
    raise SystemExit(f"Refusing to overwrite {output}; review a new candidate")
wheels = sorted(wheelhouse.glob("*.whl"))
if not wheels:
    raise SystemExit("No wheels found")
if any(p.suffix != ".whl" for p in wheelhouse.iterdir()):
    raise SystemExit("Wheel directory contains unexpected entries")
records = {}
for wheel in wheels:
    with zipfile.ZipFile(wheel) as archive:
        names = [n for n in archive.namelist() if n.endswith(".dist-info/METADATA")]
        if len(names) != 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"Ambiguous metadata: {wheel.name}")
        metadata = email.message_from_bytes(archive.read(names[0]))
    name = re.sub(r"[-_.]+", "-", metadata["Name"]).lower()
    version = metadata["Version"]
    if name in records:
        raise SystemExit(f"Duplicate distribution: {name}")
    with wheel.open("rb") as stream:
        digest = hashlib.file_digest(stream, "sha256").hexdigest()
    records[name] = f"{name}=={version} --hash=sha256:{digest}"
with output.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
    stream.write("\n".join(records[n] for n in sorted(records)) + "\n")
print(f"Wrote {len(records)} pinned wheel requirements to {output}")
4.2. Profile Preflight Validator: tools/check_profile.py
The validation engine guarantees profile purity and strict adherence to the publication contract:

import json
import os
import re
import sys
from importlib.metadata import version
from pathlib import Path

import yaml
from jupyter_client.kernelspec import KernelSpecManager

def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise SystemExit(message)

root = Path.cwd().resolve()
require(sys.implementation.name == "cpython", "CPython required")
require(sys.version_info[:3] == (3, 12, 14), "Python 3.12.14 required")
require(sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix, "Activate the project virtualenv")
for package, expected in {
    "jupyter-book": "2.1.7", "ipykernel": "7.3.0", "PyYAML": "6.0.3"
}.items():
    require(version(package) == expected, f"Wrong version: {package}")
require(version("jupyter-server"), "Jupyter Server required")
for name in ("JUPYTER_BASE_URL", "JUPYTER_TOKEN", "READTHEDOCS_CANONICAL_URL"):
    require(not os.environ.get(name), f"Unexpected environment override: {name}")
require("BASE_URL" in os.environ, "Set BASE_URL explicitly; empty is valid")
base = os.environ["BASE_URL"]
require(base == "" or (base.startswith("/") and not base.startswith("//")
        and not base.endswith("/") and not any(c in base for c in "?#\n\r")),
        "BASE_URL must be empty or a path prefix such as /docs")

kernel_dir = Path(sys.prefix) / "share/jupyter/kernels/jb2-python"
spec = json.loads((kernel_dir / "kernel.json").read_text())
require(Path(spec["argv"][0]).absolute() == Path(sys.executable).absolute(),
        "Kernel does not launch this environment's Python")
resolved = KernelSpecManager().get_kernel_spec("jb2-python")
require(Path(resolved.resource_dir).resolve() == kernel_dir.resolve(),
        "Another kernelspec overrides the project kernel")

def local_file(value):
    require(isinstance(value, str), "Source path must be a string")
    path = root / value
    require(not Path(value).is_absolute(), f"Absolute source path: {value}")
    require(path.resolve().is_relative_to(root), f"External path: {value}")
    require(path.is_file(), f"Missing source or asset: {value}")
    return path

config = yaml.safe_load(Path("myst.yml").read_text())
require(isinstance(config, dict) and config.get("version") == 1,
        "Expected myst.yml version: 1")
require("extends" not in config, "Configuration inheritance needs a profile extension")
project = config.get("project", {})
require(not project.get("plugins"), "Custom plugins need a profile extension")
require(not project.get("exclude"), "Project exclusions are not accepted")
toc = project.get("toc")
require(isinstance(toc, list) and toc, "Explicit nonempty project.toc required")
site = config.get("site", {})
require(site.get("template") == "book-theme", "Expected book-theme selector")
local_file(site.get("options", {}).get("logo"))
files = []

def walk(entries):
    require(isinstance(entries, list), "TOC children must be a list")
    for entry in entries:
        require(isinstance(entry, dict), "TOC entry must be a mapping")
        require(set(entry) <= {"file", "title", "children"},
                "Unsupported TOC entry; use file/title/children")
        require("file" in entry or entry.get("children"), "Empty TOC entry")
        if "file" in entry:
            files.append(local_file(entry["file"]))
        if "children" in entry:
            walk(entry["children"])

walk(toc)
require(len({p.resolve() for p in files}) == len(files), "Duplicate TOC file")
for path in Path("notebooks").rglob("*.ipynb"):
    if ".ipynb_checkpoints" not in path.parts:
        require(path.resolve() in {p.resolve() for p in files},
                f"Notebook absent from TOC: {path}")

banned = {"skip-execution", "raises-exception"}

def check_controls(value, label):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        execute = value.get("execute")
        if isinstance(execute, dict):
            require(execute.get("skip") in (None, False), f"Execution skipped: {label}")
        tags = value.get("tags", [])
        if isinstance(tags, (list, str)):
            require(not any(tag in tags for tag in banned), f"Forbidden tag: {label}")
        for child in value.values():
            check_controls(child, label)
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for child in value:
            check_controls(child, label)

def check_kernel(metadata, label):
    expected = {"name": "jb2-python", "display_name": "Python (JB2)", "language": "python"}
    actual = metadata.get("kernelspec", {})
    require(all(actual.get(k) == v for k, v in expected.items()),
            f"Wrong or absent kernelspec: {label}")

check_controls(config, "myst.yml")
for path in files:
    if path.suffix == ".ipynb":
        notebook = json.loads(path.read_text())
        check_controls(notebook.get("metadata", {}), path)
        cells = notebook.get("cells", [])
        for cell in cells:
            check_controls(cell.get("metadata", {}), path)
        computational = any(c.get("cell_type") == "code" for c in cells)
        computational = computational or any(
            "{ev" "al}" in "".join(c.get("source", []))
            or "{code-" "cell}" in "".join(c.get("source", []))
            for c in cells if c.get("cell_type") == "markdown")
        if computational:
            check_kernel(notebook.get("metadata", {}), path)
    elif path.suffix == ".md":
        text = path.read_text()
        front = re.match(r"\A---\r?\n(.*?)\r?\n---(?:\r?\n|\Z)", text, re.S)
        metadata = yaml.safe_load(front.group(1)) or {} if front else {}
        require(isinstance(metadata, dict), f"Invalid frontmatter: {path}")
        check_controls(metadata, path)
        if "{code-" "cell}" in text or "{ev" "al}" in text:
            check_kernel(metadata, path)
            require(not any(tag in text for tag in banned),
                    f"Review executable Markdown execution controls: {path}")
require(not Path("_config.yml").exists() and not Path("_toc.yml").exists(),
        "Remove legacy configuration from this profile")
print(f"Preflight passed for {len(files)} TOC files")

5. Continuous Deployment: .github/workflows/deploy.yml
The CI/CD pipeline deploys the publication to GitHub Pages on every push to main:

name: Jupyter Book Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pages: read
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Configure Pages
        id: pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@45bfe0192ca1faeb007ade9deae92b16b8254a0d

      - name: Configure Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97
        with:
          python-version: '3.12.14'
          architecture: x64

      - name: Install locked environment
        run: |
          python -c 'import sys; assert sys.implementation.name == "cpython" and sys.version_info[:3] == (3, 12, 14), sys.version'
          python -m venv .venv
          .venv/bin/python -m pip --version
          .venv/bin/python -m pip install \
            --require-hashes \
            --only-binary=:all: \
            -r requirements.lock
          .venv/bin/python -m pip check
          .venv/bin/python -m ipykernel install \
            --sys-prefix \
            --name jb2-python \
            --display-name 'Python (JB2)'

      - name: Validate and build publication artifact
        env:
          BASE_URL: ${{ steps.pages.outputs.base_path }}
          JB_ALLOW_NODEENV: '0'
        run: |
          . .venv/bin/activate
          sh tools/build.sh

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@fc324d3547104276b827a68afc52ff2a11cc49c9
        with:
          path: ./_build/html

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy accepted artifact
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@368f82528645a54fb793d4d04e342629a3f51346
6. Deterministic Dependency Resolution
To guarantee binary compatibility with the Ubuntu CI runner, requirements.lock was generated inside a Linux/x86-64 container hosting CPython 3.12.14:

python3.12 -m venv .lock-venv
mkdir .wheelhouse
.lock-venv/bin/python -m pip download \
    --only-binary=:all: \
    --dest .wheelhouse \
    -r requirements.in
.lock-venv/bin/python tools/lock_from_wheels.py .wheelhouse requirements.lock
rm -rf .lock-venv .wheelhouse
The resulting lockfile pins all 77 binary distributions with SHA-256 hashes, ensuring that every build step is completely isolated and reproducible.
